headline: Prices for a typical Vaughan home are down about 5% from a year ago, and the Bank of Canada raised its rate on Oct. 28. Builders have 89 active VMC applications, but fewer new projects are starting. Buyers have more choice and more room to bargain, while borrowing costs have stopped falling.

status.label: Many plans, fewer starts
status.explanation: There are 89 active VMC applications, with about 17,363 units in active site plans. But Vaughan units under construction fell to 3,144 from 3,588 a year ago, and the peak was 9,815.

status.label: Buyers cautious, rebound in new condos
status.explanation: Vaughan had 263 resale deals in October 2026, with 4.8 months of inventory. Across the GTHA, new condo sales rose 52% to 702 units in Q2 2026, but from a 35-year low.

status.label: Typical prices down 5%
status.explanation: The benchmark price of a typical Vaughan home is $1,106,600, down 5.46% from a year ago. A typical condo apartment is $504,900, down 6.51%.

status.label: Rents flat to lower
status.explanation: Average rent in the wider Richmond Hill/Vaughan/King zone was $1,726 in 2025, down from $1,762 in 2024, with a 2.4% vacancy rate. This zone is bigger than the VMC.

status.label: Rate hike, tax relief
status.explanation: The policy rate rose to 2.5% from 2.25% a year ago. The posted 5-year mortgage rate is 6.19%. Ontario's expanded HST relief on new homes and lower development charges work the other way.

personas.bottom_line: Prices are lower than a year ago, but borrowing costs just went up, so the monthly payment matters more than the sticker price.

points.text: A typical Vaughan condo apartment costs $504,900, down 6.51% from a year ago.
Ontario says expanded HST relief on new homes could save eligible buyers, including first-time buyers, up to $130,000. Check the rules for your own case.
The Bank of Canada raised its rate to 2.5% on Oct. 28 and said more increases may be needed.

watch: Bank of Canada decision on Dec. 9

personas.bottom_line: Rents in the wider zone are flat to lower, with some choice for tenants.

points.text: Average rent in the Richmond Hill/Vaughan/King zone was $1,726 in 2025, versus $1,917 in the Toronto area.
Vacancy in that zone was 2.4% in 2025. These are zone numbers, not VMC-only numbers.

personas.bottom_line: More choice and lower prices help, but higher rates and a thin pipeline of new homes cut the other way.

points.text: A typical Vaughan townhouse costs $714,500, down 8.85% from a year ago; a detached home costs $1,482,000, down 5.35%.
Vaughan has 4.8 months of resale inventory, which gives buyers more time than in tight markets.

personas.bottom_line: Prices are below last year and well below the 2022 peak, so selling conditions are softer.

points.text: The typical Vaughan home price is $1,106,600, against a peak of $1,587,400 in March 2022.
Homes sold for about 97% of the asking price in October 2026.
Developers hold a record 5,001 finished but unsold condo units across the GTHA, which can compete with resale condos.

personas.bottom_line: Lower prices and a cooling market come with higher borrowing costs and a large supply of new condos, so returns are uncertain.

points.text: The posted 5-year mortgage rate is 6.19%, versus 6.09% a year ago.
Rents in the wider zone slipped from $1,762 to $1,726 between 2024 and 2025.
Vaughan finished 6,368 units in 2025, which adds rental and resale supply.

personas.bottom_line: Sellers of larger homes are getting less than a year ago, but condos cost less too.

points.text: A typical detached home is $1,482,000 (down 5.35%); a typical condo apartment is $504,900 (down 6.51%).
Vaughan had 419 active condo apartment listings in October 2026, so there are many choices.

scenarios.name: optimistic
scenarios.summary: Rates stop rising, buyers return, and more VMC projects start building.

assumptions.assumption: Holds at 2.5% or lower through 2027, with no further hikes after Oct. 28
Expanded HST relief on new homes runs for its one-year term and boosts new condo sales

drivers.text: Lower development charges can improve project math for builders.
New condo sales rose 52% in Q2 2026 from a very low base.

scenarios.name: base
scenarios.summary: Prices stay soft and the market moves sideways, while approved projects slowly move toward construction.

assumptions.assumption: Vaughan units under construction stay near 3,100 to 3,500 rather than returning to the 9,815 peak

drivers.text: Resale prices in Vaughan are down about 5% from a year ago.

scenarios.name: pessimistic
scenarios.summary: More rate hikes and weak buyer demand push prices lower and delay new projects.

assumptions.assumption: Rises above 3.0% by the end of 2027
Unsold finished condos in the GTHA stay above 5,000 units

drivers.text: The Bank said more rate increases could be needed.
A record stock of finished, unsold condos weighs on new launches.

baseline_views.reason: Prices are drifting down and the rate hike is a modest headwind, which fits the baseline trend.
No cited evidence supports a break from the damped trend; a further rate hike adds downside risk.
Condo prices fell 6.51% in a year, and the baseline of no change is a reasonable midpoint.
Record unsold condo inventory points to soft prices, in line with the baseline's slight decline.
Starts are lumpy; 1,243 units were started in 2026 through September.
Apartment starts swing a lot year to year, and no cited evidence says otherwise.
Units under construction fell from 3,588 to 3,144 in a year as completions outpaced starts.
Zone rents slipped in 2025 and vacancy is 2.4%, so a large rise looks unlikely.

events.title: GTHA new condo sales rebound from 35-year low

events.title: Ontario expands HST relief on new homes
events.impact: Eligible buyers could save up to $130,000 on new homes for one year, which can help new condo sales.

events.title: Development Charge Reduction Program
events.impact: Municipalities need to cut development charges by 30% to 50% or more for 3 years as part of an $8.8 billion partnership.
